1.1.handover:
# 1.1 Reject configuration keys with the wrong case

## What landed

- `config: reject keys with the wrong case` — `config.Load` now validates every
  top-level key from `toml.MetaData.Keys()` against the exact spellings `dir`,
  `kinds`, `areas`, instead of relying on `Undecoded`, which misses keys the
  decoder matched case-insensitively. Rejected keys are quoted in the error.
- `TestLoadRejectsCaseVariantKeys` covers `Kinds`, `Dir`, `AREAS`, an unrelated
  `foo`, and acceptance of all three lowercase keys with their values.

## Landmark drift

None. `internal/config/config.go` and `config_test.go` are where the work order
said.

## Deviations from the work order

None. The unknown-key error keeps its existing wording and now names every
rejected key, comma-separated.

## What the next session must know

- `meta.Keys()` includes key groups, so a nested key fails the `len(key) != 1`
  check and its dotted `key.String()` is reported. `Undecoded` is no longer
  used.
- `DESIGN.md` already promises an unknown key is an error and lists the three
  lowercase keys, so no design change was needed.
- Both `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None.

commits: 38fc30f835627111f2497ae3eca58edffa005c00 config: skip directory impostors in root discovery

# 1.2 Walk past a directory named like the configuration file

## What landed

- `config: skip directory impostors in root discovery` — `FindRoot` now requires
  `os.Stat` to report a regular file (which follows symlinks) before choosing a
  root; anything else, including a directory named `.benchpress.toml`, is
  skipped and discovery continues upward.
- `TestFindRootSkipsConfigDirectory` covers a real config above an impostor
  directory and `ErrNoRoot` when only the impostor exists.
  `TestFindRootFollowsConfigSymlink` pins the symlink-to-regular-file behavior.

## Landmark drift

None. `internal/config/config.go:63` was still `FindRoot`, and the check was
the `os.Stat` at the former line 69.

## Deviations from the work order

None. `os.Stat` already followed symlinks, so `Mode().IsRegular()` on its result
covers both parts of the goal without `Lstat` or `os.Readlink`.

## What the next session must know

- Non-regular files (FIFOs, devices, sockets) now also fail to mark a root;
  that follows from the "regular file" wording and is not separately tested.
- No DESIGN change: §2's "first directory holding `.benchpress.toml`" already
  implies a file, and no format, command, key, lint rule or package boundary
  changed.
- Both `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None.

commits: 4a97afcb25bcaf98a8d9c53d16c9f507b4f7df07 topic: preserve CRLF on append and reject empty titles
1.3.handover:
# 1.3 Preserve CRLF when appending a field and reject empty titles

## What landed

- `topic: preserve CRLF on append and reject empty titles` — when the closing
  `---` has no terminator, `Set` now takes the preceding line's terminator
  before falling back to LF. `Parse` reports a `title` issue for a level-one
  heading whose text is empty or whitespace-only, while still counting that
  heading for the multiple-H1 check.
- `TestSetAppendCRLFWithoutFinalNewline` pins populated and empty CRLF front
  matter with an unterminated closing delimiter, byte for byte.
  `TestParseEmptyTitle` covers `#` and `#   ` at line 7.

## Landmark drift

None. `Set`, `terminator`, `heading1` and `Parse` are still in
`internal/topic/topic.go`; the append fallback was at the former lines 179-181
and the heading acceptance at 317-321.

## Deviations from the work order

- DESIGN also changed, as the execution rules require for a lint-rule change:
  §3 says an empty level-one heading is not a title, and §6's `title` row now
  names it.
- `Parse` still assigns the empty heading text to `Title`/`TitleLine` so the
  issue's line stays exact; the topic is not valid because the `title` issue
  is present. Callers already treat an empty title as no title (`nextText`
  falls back to the slug).

## What the next session must know

- The fallback order is: closing line's terminator, else the preceding line's,
  else LF. The LF branch is effectively unreachable through `splitLines` for a
  closed front matter, but kept for the stated contract.
- The empty-title issue is only emitted for the first heading. Empty later
  headings still produce just the existing "more than one level-one heading"
  issue.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None.

commits: 91d8d182847280a772f20c308227aab8d6d17879 topic: exclude image tokens from link collection
1.4.handover:
# 1.4 Exclude image tokens from collected links

## What landed

- `topic: exclude image tokens from link collection` — `collectLinks` now
  recognizes an unescaped `![` and skips the entire image token, alt text and
  target included. `TestImagesAreNotLinks` covers `Parse` and `LineLinks` with
  an `.png` image, a `.md` image target, an image whose alt text contains a
  link, an adjacent real link, and an escaped `\!` before a real link.

## Landmark drift

None. `collectLinks`, `parseLink` and `LineLinks` are still in
`internal/topic/topic.go`; `collectLinks` was at 374-392 and is now at 374-402.
`Parse` still calls it for body lines and lint still calls `LineLinks` for Next
items (`internal/lint/lint.go:149`).

## Deviations from the work order

- Added small `imageEnd`, `closing` and `escaped` helpers rather than extending
  `parseLink`: `parseLink` stops at the first `]`, so an image with a link in
  its alt text needs bracket matching to be skipped whole. `closing` tracks
  nesting and backslash escapes; `parseLink` itself is unchanged.
- The DESIGN sentence in §3 also names Next item text, since the same collector
  governs both, while placing the statement in §3 as D1 asks.

## What the next session must know

- An escaped `\![text](target)` is not an image, so its link is collected.
- An image token whose bracket or target parenthesis is unclosed is not skipped;
  ordinary link collection then continues from its `[`. No test pins this
  malformed-input case.
- `escaped` counts the run of backslashes immediately before the byte, so even
  runs leave a following `!` unescaped.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None.

# 1.5 Separate a newly added Next block from unterminated prose

## What landed

- `next: separate added items from unterminated prose` — `Next.Render` inserts
  the source's newline before the first item when the last head line has no
  terminator. Existing head bytes are untouched; a source with no final newline
  still renders its final item without one. `TestAddAfterUnterminatedProse`
  covers Add and AddAt at 1 for LF and CRLF sources, the exact added item bytes,
  and the no-op round trip for both.

## Landmark drift

None. `Render` was at `internal/next/next.go:121` and is now at 121-137;
`Add` and `AddAt` are unchanged.

## Deviations from the work order

- The new test also asserts that parsing and rendering without an operation
  returns the source byte for byte, because the goal requires the no-operation
  round trip to stay unchanged. No new test file.

## What the next session must know

- The separator is emitted only when items exist and the last head line lacks
  `\n`; a no-item source still renders unchanged, including a completely empty
  source (empty stays empty).
- CRLF style comes from `Next.nl`, detected from the first newline in the

- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

commits: 7e579d9c22b7a2f2e53924af25962d79cfd31af7 next: preserve each item's line ending
1.6.handover:
# 1.6 Preserve each parsed Next item's line terminator

## What landed

- `next: preserve each item's line ending` — `Item` now retains its own
  terminator; `Parse` records it from the source line. `Render` writes each
  parsed item's terminator, supplies the file's detected style when an item is
  not the final output line and has none, and preserves the absent final
  newline. `Add`, `Remove`, `Move` and prose gathering are unchanged.
- `TestRoundTripMixedLineEndings` covers LF-then-CRLF, CRLF-then-LF and a
  missing final newline. `TestMoveMixedLineEndings` covers moving to the ends,
  adding in the middle, and moving a final unterminated item so it gains a
  terminator without welding.

## Landmark drift

None. The evidence lines moved as expected: `Item` is at
`internal/next/next.go:20`, `Parse` at 50, `Render` at 127.

## Deviations from the work order

- The terminator is an unexported `term string` on `Item`, not an exported
  field. It keeps `Item` comparable (existing tests compare values) and stops
  `board` from constructing items with a stale terminator; new items correctly
  fall back to the file style.
- No DESIGN change: the specified format and commands are unchanged; the fix
  preserves bytes the design already says are kept.

## What the next session must know

- `Render` treats the last item as the final output line only when no tail
  lines follow. If the source had no final newline, the final output line is
  rendered without one even when that item carried a terminator from an
  earlier position; this preserves the existing missing-final-newline behavior.
- Terminators are carried by `Move` and by `Remove` because the `Item` value
  moves intact. `Add`/`AddAt` receive items with an empty term, which `Render`
  fills with `n.nl`, detected from the first newline in the source.
- Tests live in `internal/next/next_test.go`.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None.

2.1.handover:
# 2.1 Read literal paths and full branch refs from git

## What landed

- `repo: read literal paths and full branch refs` — `branches` asks
  `for-each-ref` for `%(refname)`, so it returns full `refs/heads/...` refs.
  `branchHolds` passes the full ref to `ls-tree`; `Find` strips `refs/heads/`
  only when appending the branch name to its result.
- `branchHolds` now runs `ls-tree -r -z --name-only` and splits on NUL, so
  non-ASCII and otherwise unusual paths are matched literally instead of
  C-quoted.
- DESIGN §5 records `%(refname)`, `-z`, and the internal-full/display-short
  split.
- New tests `TestFindNonASCIIPlanOnBranch` and
  `TestFindBranchNameWithTagCollision` reproduce both defects before the fix.

## Landmark drift

None. `branches` is at `internal/repo/repo.go:101`, `branchHolds` at 112,
`Find` at 54; the evidence line numbers in the work order had already moved
with earlier edits.

## Deviations from the work order

- The collision test creates branch `heads/foo` from `main` at the seed commit,
  so it does not hold the plan. The expected result is only `foo`; had
  `heads/foo` held the plan, `heads/foo` would be a legitimate displayed name.
- Unit 2.2's D2 error classification was left untouched, as this unit did not
  cite it. `Find` still swallows any `for-each-ref` error as "outside a repo".

## What the next session must know

- `branches` returns full refs. Any future caller adding a third git command
  should keep the same internal/display split.
- `nonEmptyLines` is still used only for `for-each-ref` output; branch names
  cannot contain newlines, so newline splitting remains safe there.
- `strings.TrimPrefix(ref, "refs/heads/")` is deliberately unconditional: every
  ref comes from the `refs/heads` pattern.
- The command-count test still passes: one `for-each-ref`, one `ls-tree` per
  branch, no other subcommands.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None for this unit. Unit 2.2 still needs to surface non-repository git failures
and update DESIGN §5's error distinction.

commits: b040e35e04de36fe2c2117bf9c6316bb362a8472 repo: report git failures outside the outside-repo case
2.2.handover:
# 2.2 Surface repository failures without breaking operation outside git

## What landed

- `repo: report git failures outside the outside-repo case` — the git runner
  now sets `LC_ALL=C`, captures stderr and returns a `gitError` carrying the
  command, stderr and process error. Only stderr beginning
  `fatal: not a git repository` is classified as the outside-repo case; `Find`
  then returns the worktree hits without error. Every other branch-enumeration
  failure is propagated with its diagnostic.
- Cancellation before a command start returns `ctx.Err()` directly.
- New tests: `TestFindCorruptRefsReturnsError` (malformed packed-refs),
  `TestFindDoesNotSuppressOtherFailures` (pre-cancelled context and no `git` on
  `PATH`). `TestFindOutsideRepository` is unchanged and still passes.
- DESIGN §5 documents `LC_ALL=C`, retained stderr, the exact outside-repo
  diagnostic, and propagation of all other failures.

## Landmark drift

Evidence cited `internal/repo/repo.go:63-75,98-103`; after unit 2.1 the runner is
at the `New` literal (now ~64-95), `Find` at ~97 and `branches` at ~145.

## Deviations from the work order

- Added `withoutLocale`, which removes an inherited `LC_ALL` before appending
  `LC_ALL=C`. On Unix a duplicate `LC_ALL` is not reliably overridden.
- The cancellation test cancels before the call; that exercises the explicit
  `ctx.Err()` pre-check. Cancellation mid-command still propagates the process
  error (typically `signal: killed`), not necessarily `context.Canceled`.
- On a non-outside-repo failure `Find` returns the partial worktree map along
  with the error; callers in `lint` and `cmd` discard the map when err != nil.

## What the next session must know

- `errNotRepository` is package-private and matched via `errors.Is` through
  `gitError.Is`. Do not switch to matching exit code 128; other fatal errors
  also use 128.
- `gitError.Unwrap` preserves the original `*exec.ExitError` / `*exec.Error`, so
  `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` only holds for the pre-check path.
- `New` is the only place the command environment is built; test wrappers that
  replace `r.run` bypass the locale and stderr behavior.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None for this unit. The plan's next stage unit (2.3, lint) is not started.

commits: b1c03b214d9fa7ae8886e00ad403792d6bf645bf Match Next targets to topic files
3.1.handover:
# 3.1 Match Next targets to the actual topic path

## What landed

- `board: Match Next targets to topic files` (`b1c03b2`) replaces the two
  `targetSlug` helpers with `Board.NextSlug`, which rejects empty and absolute
  targets, requires `.md`, normalizes against `Config.Dir`, and requires the
  file's parent to be that directory.
- Listing, `NextIndex` and lint now use it, so `./a.md` and `sub/../a.md` name
  `a.md`; `a`, `sub/a.md` and `../outside/a.md` do not. Invalid items do not
  enter `nextSlugs`, do not satisfy `NextIndex`, and do not make a later
  `[A](a.md)` a duplicate.
- Tests: `TestNextTargetsMustNameTopicFiles` in board and lint covers every
  path form with present and absent subdirectory/outside files, plus invalid
  then valid; `TestLSInvalidNextTarget` checks text and JSON keep `a` in its
  area group.
- DESIGN §4 states the accepted target shape and that a non-topic target is
  not a Next position for any topic.

## Landmark drift

The evidence pointed at `internal/board/board.go:285-289` and
`internal/lint/lint.go:140,191-195`. The old board helper is gone; the new
`NextSlug` is near the end of `internal/board/board.go`. Lint's local helper is
gone and `checkNext` calls `c.board.NextSlug`.

## Deviations from the work order

- Used one exported board resolver instead of keeping both `targetSlug`
  helpers. Lint already imports board, so this keeps path normalization single
  sourced rather than duplicating the rule.
- Added the DESIGN §4 clarification although the done-when list did not name
  it, because the document defines what a Next item links to.

## What the next session must know

- `NextSlug` deliberately returns a slug for a well-shaped target even when no
  such topic is loaded. Lint needs that to keep distinguishing
  `links to "b.md", not a topic` from `links to missing topic "b"`; board
  Listing and `nextIndex` apply the loaded-topic check at their own call sites.
- An invalid item already in NEXT.md is left untouched by add/remove/move for
  the topic it superficially resembles, because it never belonged to that
  topic.
- `scripts/verify` and `go test ./...` were green before the commit.

## Open problems

None.
